AnimeGANv3 pretrained face generators by TachibanaYoshino
(https://github.com/TachibanaYoshino/AnimeGANv3):

  AnimeGANv3_JP_face.onnx        — via huggingface.co/vumichien/AnimeGANv3_JP_face
                                   (mirror of the author's face model)
  AnimeGANv3_PortraitSketch.onnx — via huggingface.co/public-data/
                                   AnimeGANv3-portrait-sketch (PortraitSketch_25)
  *_fp16.onnx                    — the same weights in float16 (served to the
                                   WebGPU execution provider)

The network weights are unmodified apart from float16 rounding in the fp16
variants. The graphs were mechanically converted for browser execution
(opset 9 → 17, deprecated Upsample → Resize with asymmetric coordinates,
constant-folded x2 resize scales, decomposed tf.nn.moments normalization
fused into InstanceNormalization / ReduceMean, onnxslim) and verified
numerically against the originals on the CPU execution provider
(fp32: max|Δ| ≤ 2e-5, fp16: mean|Δ| ≈ 2e-3).

These weights are NOT covered by this repository's MIT license. They are
made freely available for NON-COMMERCIAL purposes only (academic research,
teaching, personal use). For commercial use you must obtain an
authorization letter from the author — see the AnimeGANv3 repository
README for contact details.

They are bundled here solely so the anime.html demo can run same-origin
in the browser. The fluent_scene engine itself does not link or contain
them.

---

id_lineart.onnx / id_lineart_fp16.onnx — "Informative Drawings" line
drawing generator (Chan, Durand, Isola: "Learning to Generate Line
Drawings that Convey Geometry and Semantics", 2022).
https://github.com/carolineec/informative-drawings — **MIT license**.
ONNX export via huggingface.co/rocca/informative-drawings-line-art-onnx;
fp16 variant is the same weights rounded to float16.

---

tiny_lines.onnx / tiny_lines_fp16.onnx — **our own weights, MIT license**
(same terms as this repository).

A 105k-parameter line net distilled from id_lineart.onnx (Informative
Drawings, MIT — see above) by nn/distill/train.py on COCO val2017 images:
the teacher's output is the only training target, so what the weights carry
is the teacher's style, not the photographs. Because the teacher is MIT,
these distilled weights are ours to license as MIT — unlike the AnimeGANv3
models above, they carry no non-commercial restriction.

~40x smaller and ~10x faster than the teacher (512² CPU: 12ms multi-threaded
/ 92ms single-threaded on a Ryzen desktop, vs 1136ms for the teacher on
Jetson Thor). The style is a lighter pencil sketch: contours are kept,
the teacher's fine hatching on flat areas is not. opset 17, dynamic HxW.

---

tiny_ink.onnx / tiny_ink_fp16.onnx — **our own weights, MIT license**
(same terms as this repository).

Same 105k architecture, same MIT teacher, but distilled against a thick-ink
target that nn/distill/ink_target.py builds from the teacher's output: the
photo is flattened with a guided filter first (so the teacher never draws
skin pores or foliage, which is where the illustration-like simplification
comes from), the surviving strokes are joined by hysteresis and dilated to
3px, and the exported graph ends in a contrast step that re-decides the
student's greys. No AnimeGANv3 weights were used, as a teacher or otherwise
— the style is ours, so these weights carry no non-commercial restriction.

The stroke width is baked in pixels, so the bold look lands at ~512²; at
1024² the same model draws a fine line drawing instead (anime.html snaps
the inference size to 512 when this model is picked).

Training record: nn/distill/runs/NOTES.md
